newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan fails to meet monetary targets in 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan fails to meet monetary targets in 1995/96.

text.p: Pakistan failed to meet its targets for restraining domestic credit and the money supply in 1995/96 (July-June), the State (central) bank of Pakistan (SBP) said in its annual report released on Thursday.
The central bank blamed excessive government borrowing as the main factor for a 20 percent jump in domestic credit, compared to a revised target of 14.3 percent.

It said a drawdown of net foreign assets in the banking system had held back growth in money supply to 14.9 percent, compared to 16.6 percent in 1994/95, but this still exceeded the 1995/96 target of 12.1 percent, the report said.
It said Pakistan's "intermediate" goals were to cut domestic credit growth to 11.1 percent and monetary growth to 13.1 percent, but did not say how soon these were to be achieved.
"The achievement of these ambitious targets would require sustained effort to implement prudent fiscal, monetary and exchange rate policies," the SBP said.
